analysis: The question requires identifying which of the listed drugs is an uricosuric agent. Uricosuric drugs are characterized by their ability to increase the excretion of uric acid in the urine, thus lowering blood uric acid levels. Among the options provided, Probenecid is well-known and widely recognized in medical literature as an uricosuric drug. It functions by inhibiting the reabsorption of uric acid in the kidneys, thereby increasing its excretion. Allopurinol, on the other hand, works by a different mechanism: it inhibits xanthine oxidase, thereby reducing the production of uric acid, and is not classified as uricosuric. Indomethacin and Aspirin are primarily anti-inflammatory drugs; while Aspirin can have a complex effect on uric acid depending on the dose, it is not primarily used as an uricosuric agent. Therefore, based on the standard medical knowledge and consensus, Probenecid is the correct answer.
